## Article

- Citation and DOI: Castiello, S., Pitliya, R. J., Lametti, D. R., et al. (2026). Affiliation in
  human-AI interactions is based on shared psychological traits. *Communications Psychology, 4*,
  93. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s44271-026-00433-8>
- Data/materials repository URL: <https://github.com/santiagocdo/chatPersonalities>
- Part A (known case) or Part B (a classmate's project paper): Part B
- Part B only: the classmate's project repo, and which target outcome is its key effect: <https://github.com/psych251/castiello2026>
The key effect is target 1, the mirror vs inverse paired t-test.

## Materials inventory

Filled in after obtaining the data and code.

| Item | Available? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw data | Partly | `experiment3/` holds the participant table from the study platform (`2025_gptstudyusers_bfi.csv`, 119 sign-ups, 100 marked `Include data = 1`), the chatbot order file, and every chat message with a sentiment label already attached (`gpt_data_all_bfi.csv`, 5,626 messages from 117 users). Item-level BFI-44 answers for the main sample are not included, only scored trait means. The sentiment labels arrive pre-computed, so that labelling step cannot be rerun from the repo. Item-level BFI data exist only for the pilot (`experiment3/pilot/`). |
| Processed data | Yes | `2025_gpt_bfi_scores.csv` (trait means, 1 to 5, 116 people), `2025_gpt_pcq_bfi.csv` (the six post-chat ratings for each chatbot, already limited to the 100 included participants). `experiment3/study1/` looks like an earlier partial export (49 rated participants). |
| Codebook / variable descriptions | No | The README says which script goes with which experiment and documents the Experiment 1 and 2 platform nodes, but there is no variable list for Experiment 3. Column names are readable (e.g. `chat_again_mirror`). Gender is coded 1, 2, 3 with no key. `BigFive44_scoring.csv` gives the BFI-44 item-to-trait key and reverse-scored items (its `question` column is empty). |
| Analysis code | Yes | `main_e3.R` (Experiment 3, Figure 4) plus `functions.R` (`summariseChatInteraction_e3`, used for the sentiment counts). Paths are relative to the repo root (it is an RStudio project). The script does not run from top to bottom as is: line 453 uses `print_fig`, which is only defined in `main.R`. Statistics come from `report::report_table()`, so the exact numbers depend on the versions of `report`, `effectsize` and `parameters`, and the repo does not record them. |
| Preregistration | Yes | <https://aspredicted.org/9yg6-y3xp.pdf> (cited in the article, dated 23 June 2025). The repo also has the Word text (`asPredicted_v2.docx`) and the power analysis (`sample_size_calculation_exp3.R`). |

## Reproduction

The agent's work, under your direction. Keep all code visible.

The code below follows the steps in the authors' `main_e3.R` (and `functions.R` for the
sentiment counts), rewritten with tidyverse. It reads the repo's files from
`chatPersonalities/` and does not change them. For the mixed models and effect sizes it uses the
same functions the authors used (`lmerTest::lmer`, `report::report_table`, which calls
`effectsize` and `parameters`).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(lmerTest)   # lmer() with Satterthwaite df, as in main_e3.R
library(report)     # report_table(), as in main_e3.R

data_dir <- "chatPersonalities/experiment3"

# package versions matter for the effect size CIs, so print them
sapply(c("lme4", "lmerTest", "report", "effectsize", "parameters"),
       \(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)))

# helper for the paper vs reproduced comparison tables
show <- function(...) knitr::kable(tibble(...))
```

```{r}
#| label: load
bfi     <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "2025_gpt_bfi_scores.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ratings <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "2025_gpt_pcq_bfi.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
users   <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "2025_gptstudyusers_bfi.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
chats   <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "gpt_data_all_bfi.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

c(bfi_rows = nrow(bfi), rated_participants = n_distinct(ratings$participant_ID),
  users_included = sum(users$`Include data` %in% 1), chat_messages = nrow(chats),
  chat_users = n_distinct(chats$userid))

# every rated participant is one of the 100 marked "Include data = 1"
all(ratings$participant_ID %in% users$participant_ID[users$`Include data` %in% 1])
```

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
traits <- c("extraversion_score", "agreeableness_score", "conscientiousness_score",
            "openness_score", "neuroticism_score")

# Personality distance between the two chatbots (main_e3.R lines 10-42).
# Traits are moved from 1..5 to -2..+2; the inverse bot is the sign-flipped profile.
# pers_distance = -(x . -x) = sum(x^2).
bfi <- bfi |>
  mutate(across(all_of(traits), \(x) x - 3)) |>
  mutate(pers_distance = rowSums(across(all_of(traits), \(x) x^2)))

# Affiliation score (main_e3.R lines 79-175): each of the six 1..5 ratings minus 3,
# "different" and "distant" reversed, then averaged per participant and chatbot.
# The long format keeps the authors' column order so that the averages are computed
# in the same order (this matters for target 2, see below).
aff <- ratings |>
  pivot_longer(-participant_ID, names_to = "item", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(chat     = if_else(str_detect(item, "mirror"), "mirror", "inverse"),
         response = value - 3,
         likerts  = if_else(str_detect(item, "different|distant"), -response, response)) |>
  group_by(participant_ID, chat) |>
  summarise(likerts = mean(likerts), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(bfi, participant_ID, pers_distance), by = "participant_ID")

# one row per participant, mirror and inverse side by side
aff_wide <- aff |>
  select(participant_ID, chat, likerts) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = chat, values_from = likerts) |>
  mutate(diff = mirror - inverse)

c(participants = nrow(aff_wide), missing_distance = sum(is.na(aff$pers_distance)))
```

### Target 1: paired t-test, mirror vs inverse (key effect)

```{r}
#| label: target1
t1  <- t.test(aff_wide$mirror, aff_wide$inverse, paired = TRUE)
t1r <- report_table(t1)   # what main_e3.R line 196 prints
d1  <- effectsize::cohens_d(aff_wide$mirror, aff_wide$inverse, paired = TRUE)
t1r

show(statistic = c("t", "df", "p", "Cohen's d", "d 95% CI"),
     paper      = c("5.66", "99", "< .001", "0.57", "[0.36, 0.78]"),
     reproduced = c(sprintf("%.2f", t1$statistic), t1$parameter, format.pval(t1$p.value, 3),
                    sprintf("%.2f", d1$Cohens_d),
                    sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", d1$CI_low, d1$CI_high)),
     unrounded  = c(sprintf("%.4f", t1$statistic), "", sprintf("%.2e", t1$p.value),
                    sprintf("%.4f", d1$Cohens_d),
                    sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]", d1$CI_low, d1$CI_high)))
```

### Target 2: Wilcoxon signed rank test

The value of V depends on how ties among the mirror minus inverse differences are ranked. The
affiliation scores are means of six integers, so many differences should be exactly equal, but
floating-point rounding makes some of them differ in the last digits. Then `wilcox.test()` ranks
them as different values. The table shows V as the authors' code computes it (same order of
averaging as `main_e3.R`; running the first 207 lines of `main_e3.R` itself also gives 3601.5),
V when the averages are taken in a different order, and V when the scores are rounded to 8
decimals so that equal differences really are tied.

```{r}
#| label: target2
wx_authors <- wilcox.test(aff_wide$mirror, aff_wide$inverse, paired = TRUE)
wx_authors   # "Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction", as quoted in the paper

# same scores, averaged in a different item order
alt_score <- function(cond) {
  r <- ratings
  rowMeans(cbind(r[[paste0("chat_again_", cond)]], r[[paste0("enjoy_", cond)]],
                 r[[paste0("similar_", cond)]], r[[paste0("understood_", cond)]],
                 6 - r[[paste0("different_", cond)]], 6 - r[[paste0("distant_", cond)]]) - 3)
}
alt <- tibble(participant_ID = ratings$participant_ID,
              mirror_alt = alt_score("mirror"), inverse_alt = alt_score("inverse")) |>
  left_join(aff_wide, by = "participant_ID")
max(abs(alt$mirror_alt - alt$mirror))   # the scores agree to within rounding error
wx_alt     <- wilcox.test(alt$mirror_alt, alt$inverse_alt, paired = TRUE)
wx_rounded <- wilcox.test(round(aff_wide$mirror, 8), round(aff_wide$inverse, 8), paired = TRUE)

show(version    = c("paper", "authors' averaging order", "other averaging order",
                    "rounded (exact ties)"),
     V          = c("3600", wx_authors$statistic, wx_alt$statistic, wx_rounded$statistic),
     p          = c("< .001", format.pval(c(wx_authors$p.value, wx_alt$p.value,
                                            wx_rounded$p.value), 3)))
```

### Target 3: chatbot × personality distance interaction

`main_e3.R` line 230 fits `lmer(likerts ~ chat*pers_distance + (1|participant_ID))`. R makes
`inverse` the reference level (alphabetical), so the interaction term is "mirror minus inverse
slope". The paper's β3 is negative but its standardized coefficient is positive, so the model is
fitted below with both reference levels.

```{r}
#| label: target3
m3 <- lmer(likerts ~ chat * pers_distance + (1 | participant_ID), data = aff)
m3_mirror_ref <- lmer(likerts ~ chat * pers_distance + (1 | participant_ID),
                      data = mutate(aff, chat = relevel(factor(chat), ref = "mirror")))

summary(m3)$coefficients
summary(m3_mirror_ref)$coefficients

# standardized coefficient as report_table() computes it (refit on standardized data)
std3 <- parameters::standardize_parameters(m3, method = "refit")
std3

b3 <- summary(m3)$coefficients[4, ]
b3_m <- summary(m3_mirror_ref)$coefficients[4, ]
show(statistic  = c("b3 (inverse = reference, authors' code)", "b3 (mirror = reference)",
                    "p", "Std. Coef.", "Std. Coef. 95% CI"),
     paper      = c("-0.09", "-0.09", ".045", "0.26", "[0.01, 0.51]"),
     reproduced = c(sprintf("%.2f", b3["Estimate"]), sprintf("%.2f", b3_m["Estimate"]),
                    sprintf("%.3f", b3["Pr(>|t|)"]), sprintf("%.2f", std3$Std_Coefficient[4]),
                    sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", std3$CI_low[4], std3$CI_high[4])))
```

### Target 4: share of participants who affiliated more with the mirror chatbot

```{r}
#| label: target4
count(aff_wide, direction = case_when(diff > 0 ~ "mirror higher",
                                      diff < 0 ~ "inverse higher",
                                      TRUE ~ "tie"))
show(statistic = "% with mirror > inverse", paper = "64%",
     reproduced = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(aff_wide$diff > 0)))
```

### Target 5: sentiment of participants' messages × chatbot condition

Following `summariseChatInteraction_e3()` in `functions.R`: punctuation and spaces are removed
from the sentiment labels (one message is labelled `Mixed.`), the participant's messages in
each chat are counted by sentiment, the counts are turned into proportions within each chat, and
`main_e3.R` line 396 fits `anova(lmer(prop ~ sentiment * botcondition + (1|participant_ID)))`.

```{r}
#| label: target5
sentiments <- c("Mixed", "Negative", "Neutral", "Positive")
table(chats$usersentiment)

user_sent <- chats |>
  filter(userid %in% ratings$participant_ID) |>
  mutate(sentiment = factor(str_remove_all(usersentiment, "[[:punct:] ]"), levels = sentiments)) |>
  count(participant_ID = userid, botcondition = botpersonality, sentiment, .drop = FALSE) |>
  complete(participant_ID, botcondition, sentiment, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  group_by(participant_ID, botcondition) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()
c(rows = nrow(user_sent), participants = n_distinct(user_sent$participant_ID))

a5  <- anova(lmer(prop ~ sentiment * botcondition + (1 | participant_ID), data = user_sent))
a5
a5r <- report_table(a5)   # partial eta squared with one-sided CI, as in main_e3.R
a5r

int <- a5["sentiment:botcondition", ]
eta <- as.data.frame(a5r)[3, ]
show(statistic  = c("df", "F", "p", "eta2 (partial)", "eta2 95% CI"),
     paper      = c("(784, 3)", "6.5", "< .001", ".02", "[.01, 1.00]"),
     reproduced = c(sprintf("(%d, %.0f)", int$NumDF, int$DenDF), sprintf("%.2f", int$`F value`),
                    format.pval(int$`Pr(>F)`, 3), sprintf("%.2f", eta$Eta2_partial),
                    sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", eta$Eta2_partial_CI_low, eta$Eta2_partial_CI_high)))
```

As a check, the authors' own function gives the same per-chat sentiment proportions:

```{r}
#| label: target5-check
source("chatPersonalities/functions.R")   # defines summariseChatInteraction_e3(); needs gtools
authors <- summariseChatInteraction_e3(as.data.frame(chats),
                                       intersect(ratings$participant_ID, chats$userid))$combine
user_cols <- paste0("user_", sentiments)
authors_props <- authors |>
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(all_of(user_cols))),
         across(all_of(user_cols), \(x) x / total)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(user_cols), names_to = "sentiment", values_to = "prop_authors",
               names_prefix = "user_")
check <- inner_join(user_sent, authors_props,
                    by = c("participant_ID", "botcondition", "sentiment"))
c(rows_matched = nrow(check), max_abs_difference = max(abs(check$prop - check$prop_authors)))
```

## Checker's verdict

Filled in by you, not the agent.

| # | Paper value | Reproduced value | Verdict (exact / minor / major / not reproducible) | Reason for discrepancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | t(99) = 5.66, p < .001, d = 0.57 [0.36, 0.78] | t(99) = 5.66, p < .001, d = 0.57 [0.35, 0.78] | minor | Possible differences in CI computation or `effectsize` version |
| 2 | V = 3600, p < .001 | V = 3601.5, p < .001 | minor | Effects of averaging order |
| 3 | β3 = −0.09, p = .045, Std. Coef. = 0.26 [0.01, 0.51] | β3 = 0.09, p = .045, Std. Coef. = 0.26 [0.01, 0.51]| minor | β3 sign inconsistent with the reported standardized coefficient (opposite reference coding) |
| 4 | 64% | 64% | exact | N/A|
| 5 | F = 6.5, p < .001, η² = .02 [.01, 1.00] | F(3, 792) = 6.50, p = .0002, η² = 0.02 [0.01, 1.00] | minor | Swapped degrees of freedom reported, and incorrect error df |

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right: Targets 1, 3, 4, and 5 reproduced, "within rounding or reporting slips." Target 2 does not match exactly: V = 3601.5 instead of 3600, though the conclusion (p < .001) holds.
The agent's claim was accurate.
